correctness.rationale: The finite cyclic multiplicative group of size 23·89 has 111 nonprimitive elements, exactly the union of the order-23 and order-89 subgroups. Four explicit GF(2)[T] Bezout identities with RHS 1 rule out all translated pairs, without extrapolating enumeration. An independent complete representation of GF(2048) via the irreducible T^11+T^2+1 confirms 2047 nonzero tests and zero pairs. For smaller composite multiplicative orders, the extension exponent is composite and a proper subfield supplies a pair. Euler phi gives theta=1936/2047, so the density-threshold obstruction follows with its stated strictness. The standalone verifier replays all critical finite identities.

value.rationale: The problem is explicitly motivated by a newly published characteristic-two existence threshold. This is the first binary extension with composite multiplicative-group order yet no nonprimitive pair, despite 111 nonprimitive elements. It disproves the natural composite-group-order sufficiency guess, isolates the additive obstruction as four exact cyclotomic coprimalities, and bounds from above the allowable theta constant for any density-only sufficient criterion (outside the known small exceptions). The exact first boundary, not merely the low computational cost, supplies its mathematical value; it is not claimed to establish the optimal global threshold.
